basic_information.official_title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION OF PARLIAMENTARY DISTRICTS IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after completion of publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Draws the region's first electoral map — 32 single-member parliamentary districts covering every province, Cotabato City and the Special Geographic Area, with the population of each district set out.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The Bangsamoro Parliament will be partly elected by district. Before anyone can vote for a district representative, the districts have to exist and their boundaries be fixed by law.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The BARMM is divided into 32 parliamentary districts, each electing one representative, drawn on population and geographical area with a minimum of 100,000 people per district.
who_will_be_affected: Every voter in the BARMM — this determines which district you vote in
Candidates for district seats in the Bangsamoro Parliament
Municipalities and barangays grouped into districts
The Special Geographic Area, which receives a single Lone District
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force from 2024. The districts were subsequently reconstituted by BAA 77 and re-apportioned by BAA 86 — read those for the map as it now stands.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: This is the map. 32 single-member districts, each electing 1 Member of Parliament, each with at least 100,000 people. Note that later acts redrew it.
in_practice: Basilan 3 · Lanao del Sur 8 · Maguindanao del Norte 4 · Maguindanao del Sur 4 · Sulu 7 · Tawi-Tawi 3 · City of Cotabato 2 · Special Geographic Area 1 lone district
Districts are apportioned on population and geographical area
Each district must comprise, as far as practicable, contiguous, compact and adjacent territory
Each district must have a population of at least 100,000
The act records a total BARMM population of 4,944,800

for_specific_groups.Voters: Your district determines whose name appears on your ballot for a district seat. The act lists every municipality and, for Cotabato City, every barangay.
for_specific_groups.Lanao del Sur: The largest allocation — 8 of the 32 districts, on a population of 1,195,518.
for_specific_groups.The Special Geographic Area: A single Lone District covering all eight of its municipalities, with a population of 215,433.
for_specific_groups.Cotabato City: Two districts, drawn at barangay level rather than by municipality.
for_specific_groups.Candidates: District boundaries define where you must run and who you must reach.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The whole BARMM as constituted when the act was passed.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: At parliamentary elections — but read the later reconstituting and apportionment acts first.
what_you_can_do: Find your municipality in the district list to see which district you fall in
Check BAA 77 and BAA 86, which reconstituted and re-apportioned the districts after this act
watch_out_for: This map has been superseded in part. BAA 77 reconstituted the parliamentary districts in 2025 and BAA 86 provided for their apportionment in 2026.
The act was passed and approved by the Chief Minister on the same day, 28 February 2024 — unusually fast.
The Special Geographic Area's Lone District lists eight municipalities, including Ligawasan, for which this registry has not identified a separate creating act alongside the seven at BAA 41–47.
Some districts sit close to the 100,000 floor, so small population changes matter.

key_terms_explained.Parliamentary district: A geographical constituency electing 1 Member of Parliament.
key_terms_explained.Single-member district: A district that returns exactly one representative.
key_terms_explained.Apportionment: Dividing seats among areas according to agreed criteria — here population and geographical area.
key_terms_explained.Contiguous, compact and adjacent: The standard test that a district should be a single connected shape rather than scattered pieces.
key_terms_explained.Special Geographic Area: The former North Cotabato barangays that voted into the BARMM in 2019, organised into municipalities by BAA 41–47.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Sha'ban 18, 1445 / 28 February 2024 and approved by the Chief Minister the same day.

benefits.headline: The region's first electoral map, with every district's population published.

direct_benefits.benefit: A defined district for every voter in the region
Published population figures for each district
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Anyone checking whether representation is equitable

direct_benefits.benefit: A dedicated seat for the Special Geographic Area
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Residents of the eight SGA municipalities

indirect_benefits: A stated minimum population per district, which limits how unequal districts may become
limitations: Superseded in part by later reconstituting and apportionment acts.
No provision for periodic redistricting within the act itself.
No standard is set for how far district populations may diverge above the minimum.

for_citizens: None. The act creates no duty — it draws boundaries.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Commission on Elections, through the Bangsamoro Electoral Office
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints or challenge procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A voter in Maluso, Basilan looks up their district: Maluso sits in Basilan's 3rd District, together with Tabuan-Lasa, Lantawan, Hadji Muhtamad and Sumisip.
A resident of the Special Geographic Area finds their municipality in the Lone District, which covers all eight SGA municipalities as one constituency.
A candidate planning a campaign in Cotabato City needs the barangay lists — the act divides the city into two districts barangay by barangay.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Title: the “Bangsamoro Parliamentary Districts Act of 2024”.
Section 2 — Policy: the Bangsamoro Parliament shall ensure the equitable representation of the inhabitants of the BARMM in the apportionment of parliamentary districts.

Section 3 — Criteria: parliamentary districts are apportioned among the provinces, cities, municipalities and other geographical areas of the BARMM based on population and geographical area. Each district shall comprise, as far as practicable, contiguous, compact and adjacent territory, and shall have a population of at least 100,000.

Section 4 — Creates 32 single-member parliamentary districts for the election of district representatives, against a stated total BARMM population of 4,944,800: Basilan 3 districts (426,207); Lanao del Sur 8 (1,195,518); Maguindanao del Norte 4 (618,421); Maguindanao del Sur 4 (723,758); Sulu 7 (1,000,108); Tawi-Tawi 3 (440,276); the City of Cotabato 2 (325,079), enumerated barangay by barangay; and the Special Geographic Areas 1 Lone District (215,433) covering Kadayangan, Kapalawan, Ligawasan, Malidegao, Nabalawag, Old Kaabakan, Pahamuddin and Tugunan. Each district is listed with its component municipalities or barangays and their populations.
Section 7 — Takes effect 15 days after completion of publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Residents of the Special Geographic Area, who gain a dedicated seat
impact.figures_note: Population figures are quoted from Section 4: a regional total of 4,944,800 across 32 districts, with a stated minimum of 100,000 per district.

related_legislation.related_note: The first parliamentary district map. It was followed by BAA 77, reconstituting the parliamentary districts, and BAA 86, providing for their apportionment — both of which should be read for the current map. The Special Geographic Area municipalities it lists were created by BAA 41–47.

implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. This map has been overtaken by BAA 77 and BAA 86; anyone relying on district boundaries should read those acts. The Lone District list includes a municipality, Ligawasan, for which this registry has not identified a separate creating act among BAA 41–47.

citizen_questions.a: Thirty-two single-member parliamentary districts, each electing one representative — though the map was later reconstituted by BAA 77 and re-apportioned by BAA 86.
On population and geographical area, with each district comprising as far as practicable contiguous, compact and adjacent territory and a population of at least 100,000.
Lanao del Sur, with 8 districts on a population of 1,195,518. Sulu has 7, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi 3 each, both Maguindanao provinces 4 each, Cotabato City 2, and the Special Geographic Area 1.

citizen_questions.q: Does the Special Geographic Area get a seat?
citizen_questions.a: Yes — a single Lone District covering all eight of its municipalities, with a population of 215,433.
Not entirely. BAA 77 reconstituted the parliamentary districts in 2025 and BAA 86 provided for their apportionment in 2026. Read those for the current position.
